Answer in exactly three short sentences, with no lists, no headings, and no jargon beyond what a typical phone user would know.

node.text: When used heavily on a hot day, a phone's battery percentage reading can drop faster than normal because the heat causes the battery to discharge more quickly.
The operating system throttles the processor when it gets too hot to prevent permanent damage to the phone's internal components and ensure the device stays functional.
This happens because high temperatures cause the battery to discharge faster and the phone to reduce performance automatically to cool down and protect itself.
